sources.author: Google Street View
observations: Near-frontal elevation (HC UK tenant). Three round-headed shop openings in a rendered ground storey; jettied first floor on timber blocks; close-studded apron; two equally wide three-light front windows on separate projecting oriels, with a recessed centre under a timber arch; tie beam with carved boss; gable with one central king post and nested chevron braces under heavy bargeboards.
North of the shop, beside NatWest, a narrow gated entrance bay with a small red-tiled roof over a set-back top window.
A dark open gap with a bin between the building and William Hill, with brick walls receding behind: the side alley. Used to scale widths and heights.

sources.author: Google Street View
observations: Love To Eat tenant; sage-grey arched shop frames on a pale render storey. The red clay main roof falls towards the alley. The distant chimney belongs to another roof, not this building.
The alley opening between the cafe and William Hill is visible; William Hill's rendered side wall rises beside it.

observations: Close north oblique: projecting oriels, recessed centre, layered mouldings and porch ironwork. The left return is largely hidden in this view; the five later supplied captures resolve it as glazed. The small roof form and brace are resolved by those views rather than inferred from this crop.

sources.author: Google satellite imagery
observations: Red clay-tile roof with its ridge running back from the street gable, a narrow red roof along the NatWest side, and a flat rooflit range behind. A dark strip separates the red roof from William Hill along the full range depth: the alley continues to the rear.

sources.author: Google imagery, supplied privately by the user
observations: Frontal and both oblique views establish equal three-light front windows, taller than the apron beneath, with glazed single-light inner canted returns on both sides of the inset central plaster panel.

Single gable king post; four straight outward-rising braces each side. Heavy layered bargeboards and small apex pendant; carved end brackets, scrollwork on the tie beam and shallow carved arch spandrels. Fine leaded quarries include repeated scalloped upper borders.
The narrow roof against NatWest has a high wall edge and one falling slope. It turns down into a hip only at the street end, with no central ridge. The entrance bay has a straight diagonal brace.
Three nearly equal shop arches with pale sage frames and one continuous transom level; small Love To Eat lettering above. The side has close-studded white panels above and sage panelled return below.

sources.author: Google imagery, supplied by user
observations: Main roof has equal front pitches, a short ridge and a rear hip. No chimney. Small north roof is much shallower than the main roof.

White middle deck, lower red pitched wing with one light, broad grey rear roof with four lights and a hatch, and a narrower higher rear roof with one elongated light. Timbering is visible on rear upper walls.
Satellite scale-bar measurements and raw image landmarks are recorded in roof-measurements.json. Main depth about 7.3 m; narrow roof depth about 3.2 m. These are image measurements, not a survey.

uncertainties: Street numbering: the user's link and Google's place name give 15 London St; Google's basemap shows an '8' label here and the old placeholder named the block 8. The asset uses 15.
The model depicts the Love To Eat shopfront visible in the supplied photos, including its small name. This is a historical appearance, not an assertion about current occupancy.
Ground-level alley width (1.32m) is a scaled estimate; any gate at the street end is not modelled because the 2011 and snag images show it open. The rear brick closure is estimated.

Front heights and projections, rear roof heights and exact rooflight sizes are calibrated estimates. Satellite roof parallax limits ground registration; hidden walls, far rear ownership and rear alley closure remain uncertain. Scroll and leaf carving is interpreted relief.
